title: Frequency kernel of a compactly supported matrix symbol
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Fix integers $m\geq1$, $p,q\geq0$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$. Give $\mathbf C^p,\mathbf C^q$ their Euclidean norms and matrices their operator norm. Let $b:\mathbf R^m\times\mathbf R^m\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf C^p,\mathbf C^q)$ be smooth. Suppose there is one compact set $K\subset\mathbf R^m$ such that $b(x,\zeta)=0$ for every $x\notin K$ and every $\zeta$, and for all multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$ there is $c_{\alpha\beta}<\infty$ with $$\|\partial_x^\alpha\partial_\zeta^\beta b(x,\zeta)\|\leq c_{\alpha\beta}(1+|\zeta|)^{r-|\beta|}\quad(x,\zeta\in\mathbf R^m).$$ Write $\widehat b_x(\theta,\zeta)=\int e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\theta}b(x,\zeta)\,dx$. For every integer $L\geq0$ there is $C_L<\infty$ such that $$\|\widehat b_x(\theta,\zeta)\|\leq C_L(1+|\theta|)^{-L}(1+|\zeta|)^r.$$ If $f:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf C^p$ is Schwartz (smooth with all derivatives rapidly decreasing), put $\widehat f(\xi)=\int e^{-2\pi i y\cdot\xi}f(y)\,dy$ and $$T_b f(x)=\int e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}b(x,2\pi\xi)\widehat f(\xi)\,d\xi.$$ This integral is absolutely convergent, $T_b f$ is smooth and supported in $K$, and $$\widehat{T_b f}(\eta)=\int\widehat b_x(\eta-\xi,2\pi\xi)\widehat f(\xi)\,d\xi.$$ Finally, $T_b f$ equals the distributional oscillatory integral $\operatorname{Op}(b)f=(2\pi)^{-m}\int e^{i(x-y)\cdot\zeta}b(x,\zeta)f(y)\,dy\,d\zeta$, where oscillatory means the limit against compactly supported smooth tests after insertion of a compactly supported smooth frequency cutoff equal to one near zero and dilated to infinity.

proof.text:
If $p=0$ or $q=0$, the symbol and output take values in zero spaces, so every assertion holds with $C_L=0$. Assume $p,q>0$. Work entrywise in the standard bases. Each scalar entry $g(x)=b_{aj}(x,\zeta)$ and each of its $x$-derivatives is smooth and supported in $K$: outside the closed set $K$ the function is identically zero on a neighbourhood. They are Schwartz by [lem-sfb-schwartz-test-inclusion-integrability]. Fix $L\geq0$. Repeatedly apply the directional derivative identity in [lem-sfb-schwartz-fourier-l2-identities] in the coordinate direction $e_k$. Induction from order zero gives
$$(2\pi i\theta_k)^L\widehat g(\theta)=\widehat{\partial_k^L g}(\theta).$$
Each entry of $\partial_k^Lb$ has absolute value bounded by $c_{Le_k,0}(1+|\zeta|)^r\mathbf1_K(x)$. The scalar integral majorant estimate bounds the last Fourier integral by $\operatorname{vol}(K)c_{Le_k,0}(1+|\zeta|)^r$. For $|\theta|\geq1$, choose $k$ with $|\theta_k|\geq |\theta|/\sqrt m$ and divide by $(2\pi|\theta_k|)^L$; for $|\theta|\leq1$, use the undifferentiated integral bound. Maximize over the finitely many $k$ and entries. Since $\|M\|\leq\sum_{a,j}|M_{aj}|$ and $|\theta|^{-L}\leq2^L(1+|\theta|)^{-L}$ for $|\theta|\geq1$, enlarging the constant proves the asserted uniform $C_L$ bound, including $L=0$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-schwartz-fourier-coordinate-rule] to each component of $f$: each component of $\widehat f$ is Schwartz. For every real $d$, the function $(1+|\xi|)^d\|\widehat f(\xi)\|$ is integrable. Indeed choose integers $M>m$ and $N>\max(d,0)+M$. The Schwartz seminorms at powers $0,N$ give $\|\widehat f(\xi)\|\leq A_N(1+|\xi|)^{-N}$, by considering $|\xi|\leq1$ and $|\xi|\geq1$. The resulting majorant is at most $C(1+|\xi|^2)^{-M/2}$, integrable by [lem-sfb-euclidean-bracket-integrable] with $s=M/2$. Apply [lem-sfb-integrable-majorant-estimate] componentwise. The same argument applies to $f$ itself. Write $w_d(\xi)=(1+|\xi|)^d\|\widehat f(\xi)\|$. Since $1+2\pi|\xi|$ and $1+|\xi|$ have a ratio bounded above and below by positive constants, the symbol estimates give
$$\|\partial_x^\gamma b(x,2\pi\xi)\widehat f(\xi)\|\leq A_\gamma w_r(\xi)$$
for every $x$. The phase has modulus one. Thus the integral defining $T_bf$ converges absolutely for every $x$.

source.place: WANTED locally: Part I §3.B, Theorem 3.6, printed p.13 (PDF p.25). Agent Fourier-kernel argument; online fetch timed out.

proof.text:
Put $F(x,\xi)=e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}b(x,2\pi\xi)\widehat f(\xi)$. The product rule gives
$$\partial_x^\alpha F(x,\xi)=e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\sum_{\gamma\leq\alpha}{\alpha\choose\gamma}(2\pi i\xi)^{\alpha-\gamma}(\partial_x^\gamma b)(x,2\pi\xi)\widehat f(\xi).$$
Its norm is bounded, uniformly for all $x$, by $A_\alpha w_{r+|\alpha|}(\xi)$; the latter is integrable by step 2. All the integrands and their Fréchet derivatives in $x$ are continuous in $\xi$, hence strongly measurable. Apply [lem-sfb-dominated-integral-frechet-derivative] over the real domain $\mathbf R^m$, viewing the complex finite-dimensional codomain as real. Its neighbourhood may be any ball about $x_0$; the preceding bound for derivatives of the next order bounds the Fréchet derivative there, and step 2 supplies integrability at $x_0$. Induction, also for the finitely many derivative components, gives derivatives of every order of $T_bf$ equal to the corresponding integrals. Each derivative is itself differentiable by the next induction step, hence continuous. Thus $T_bf$ is smooth. For $x\notin K$ the defining integrand is zero, so its support is contained in $K$.

proof.text:
For fixed $\eta$, the scalar components of the kernel
$$H_\eta(x,\xi)=e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\eta}e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}b(x,2\pi\xi)\widehat f(\xi)$$
are continuous and bounded in norm by $A\mathbf1_K(x)w_r(\xi)$. This is a product-integrable majorant: integrate the $x$ section to obtain $A\operatorname{vol}(K)w_r(\xi)$ and use step 2 and the product integrability criterion of [lem-sfb-product-fubini-integral-swap], with factors interchanged. The scalar majorant estimate then gives integrability of every component of $H_\eta$. The same bound shows $T_bf$ is integrable in $x$. Both Euclidean Lebesgue spaces are sigma-finite. Fubini interchange therefore gives
$$\widehat{T_bf}(\eta)=\int\left(\int e^{-2\pi i x\cdot(\eta-\xi)}b(x,2\pi\xi)\,dx\right)\widehat f(\xi)\,d\xi.$$
A fixed vector can be moved through a finite matrix integral entrywise. The inner matrix integral is exactly $\widehat b_x(\eta-\xi,2\pi\xi)$, which proves the claimed frequency kernel formula with an absolutely convergent right-hand side.

proof.text:
Take any $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbf R^m)$ equal to one near zero and let $R>0$. Fix $x$. The cutoff kernel in $(y,\zeta)$ is bounded by
$$C\|f(y)\|\mathbf1_{\operatorname{supp}\chi(\cdot/R)}(\zeta)(1+|\zeta|)^r.$$
The frequency factor is bounded with compact support and the $y$ factor is integrable by step 2. The product criterion and scalar majorant estimate show absolute integrability. Fubini may therefore integrate in $y$ first. By the definition of $\widehat f$, its value is $\widehat f(\zeta/(2\pi))$. Apply [lem-sfb-euclidean-jacobian-integral] entrywise to the dilation $\xi\mapsto2\pi\xi$ of $\mathbf R^m$, whose determinant is $(2\pi)^m$. The cutoff operator consequently equals
$$T_Rf(x)=\int e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}b(x,2\pi\xi)\widehat f(\xi)\chi(2\pi\xi/R)\,d\xi.$$
This computes the actual regularized double integral and cancels the prefactor $(2\pi)^{-m}$ exactly. No inversion or interchange of an unregularized $(y,\zeta)$ integral is being assumed.

source.place: WANTED locally: Part I §3.B, Theorem 3.6, printed p.13 (PDF p.25). Agent Fourier-kernel argument; online fetch timed out.

proof.text:
Let $\varphi$ be any smooth compactly supported complex test; vector-valued dual tests are handled by summing components. Put $B=\sup|\chi|<\infty$. In the $(x,\xi)$ pairing of step 5, the absolute value is bounded for every $R$ by
$$AB|\varphi(x)|\mathbf1_K(x)w_r(\xi).$$
The $x$ factor is integrable since $\varphi$ is bounded and $K$ has finite volume. The product criterion in [lem-sfb-product-fubini-integral-swap] makes this an integrable majorant on the product space, and [lem-sfb-integrable-majorant-estimate] permits Fubini for the pairing with $T_Rf$. For fixed $\xi$, $\chi(2\pi\xi/R)\to1$ as $R\to+\infty$. Apply [lem-sfb-oscillatory-cutoff-convergence] on this product space, with $E=\mathbf C$ as a real Banach space and the real at-infinity filter having countable base $R>n$. All integrands are measurable and the uniform bound is the one just proved. The limit of the pairings is the pairing with $T_bf$, by the same Fubini calculation without the cutoff. Hence every allowable frequency cutoff gives the required distributional limit, equal to $T_bf$.
